stops.note: the Marquis de Sade, lord of the château of Lacoste in Provence, wrote The 120 Days of Sodom in the Bastille in 1785 and published Justine in 1791
recorded in French dictionaries from the 1830s for cruelty that gives pleasure
the psychiatrist Richard von Krafft-Ebing made it a clinical term in his Psychopathia Sexualis (1886)
entered English through translations of Krafft-Ebing

current_meaning: pleasure, especially sexual, from inflicting pain or humiliation on others
